notable_absence.finding: This is the key near-miss finding for this round's sgcollect_info/cbcollect_info comparison. The promoted tool:cbcollect-info record states three explicit bounded-non-support facts ('does NOT collect audit logs or Eventing Application logs'), directly quoted from server-side eventing docs. This page, by contrast, describes sgcollect_info's output ENTIRELY in positive terms - a table enumerating what it DOES collect (logs, configuration, expvars, OS stats, Golang profiles) - and never states a single thing it deliberately does NOT collect. So the excludesFromCapture relation, which fit tool:cbcollect-info perfectly, has no textual support here and was not minted. This is itself evidence that the two tools, despite sharing a name pattern and stated purpose, are documented in different registers: cbcollect_info's own docs are written defensively (telling support engineers what they must gather separately), while sgcollect_info's docs are written as a simple positive inventory. Whether that reflects a real difference in the tools' actual scope (does sgcollect_info silently omit anything?) or just a documentation-style difference cannot be determined from this page alone.

cross_component_finding: This page's Log Redaction section states its redacted-hash format matches cbcollect_info's own convention directly: 'tagged contents in the redacted one should be hashed in the same way as `cbcollect_info`.' This is the ONE explicit textual link between the two tools on this page - not a statement that they are the same tool or share code, but a statement that their REDACTION HASHING SCHEME is shared/consistent. This licenses a narrow, specific relation (hasEquivalentEffectAs, scoped only to the hashing behavior) rather than a full identity claim, and is the single piece of evidence keeping tool:sgcollect-info and tool:cbcollect-info from being total strangers even though they remain separately minted. Reconciliation formalized this as tool:sgcollect-info -hasEquivalentEffectAs-> tool:cbcollect-info (see relations above).
cross_product_finding: None beyond the redaction-hashing note above.
